transcript:
This is NPR News Now.
The latest headlines every hour.
Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Louise Kievone.
On Wall Street and in the tech world, big developments today.
Chip giant Nvidia reinstated controversial president and CEO Jensen Wong.
Wall Street recovered about half of last week's losses.
And Megaspeed, the company associated with the suspected spy and tangled with Wong,
is now on a Commerce Department blacklist.
NPR's Shannon Bond reports.
The Commerce Department is adding Megaspeed to a list of companies barred from buying
advanced technology without a U.S. government license.
The Justice Department has said it's conducting a criminal investigation into allegations
Megaspeed has enabled China to illegally access Nvidia's most advanced chips.
Nvidia's CEO Jensen Wong resigned earlier this month
after reports he had an affair with a Megaspeed executive
who U.S. officials suspect was working with Chinese intelligence.
This week, Nvidia's board reversed course and reinstated Wong.
Megaspeed didn't respond to a request for comment.
It previously denied wrongdoing and said the executive left the company last year.
Shannon Bond, NPR News.
Three Russian missiles fell on its territory last week
and now Poland is asking NATO to strengthen its share of the country's air defenses.
From Brussels, Terry Schultz reports the alliance will send Poland an early warning aircraft.
After NATO ambassadors held an emergency meeting at Poland's request,
the alliance's top military commander, Alexis Grinkowicz, told Poland
he would deploy one of the alliance's shared AWACS aircraft
to help the country better defend itself against errant Russian missiles.
NATO spokesperson Alison Hart says Grinkowicz is also looking at
what other assets may be sent to Poland.
After three Russian ballistic missiles landed in the eastern part of the country Friday
without being intercepted, Polish Deputy Defense Minister Pavel Zilevsky says
the AWACS plane, one of 14 NATO has based in Germany,
will give Poland better operational awareness to respond to this kind of threat.
For NPR News, I'm Terry Schultz in Brussels.
Realtor.com says its latest study shows about a third of young adult Americans
between 18 and 34 live with their parents, and PR's Jennifer Ludden looks at the numbers.
More than 25 million Americans aged 18 to 34 live with their parents,
according to a new report by Realtor.com.
The overall share is just under its peak during the pandemic.
Most of them are under 25, but the new report finds the share of older adult children
back at home has grown in the past couple decades,
and the trend is spreading outside the most expensive cities
to places like Baltimore, Houston, Atlanta and Las Vegas.
High home prices and high mortgage rates have priced out many would-be first-time buyers.
They've also led some to move in with parents to help save up for a down payment.
Jennifer Ludden, NPR News, Washington.
The Dow was up 1,447 points, closing at $49,595. This is NPR.
The AAA expects 81 million Americans to mark Thanksgiving holidays with some kind of travel.
Nearly 6 million of them will fly.
Stormy late autumn weather is in store across the nation on the west coast.
A confluence of two things could bring flooding, rain fueled by a wide band of moisture,
and king tides expected to be among the highest tides this year.
Western Oklahoma, Texas, the Great Lakes and New England could see some snow, heavy wind and rain.
Are possible in the southeast and along the east coast.
Mushrooms are among the latest wellness supplement trends promoted online,
but how good are they? Reporter Ari Daniel takes a look.
Medicinal mushrooms are a good source of vitamin D2 and antioxidants.
Their cell walls improve gut health, and there are studies suggesting that a purified extract
from the turkey tail mushroom slightly improved the survival rate in cancer patients
who'd undergone surgical removal of a gastric tumor and chemotherapy.
But there's still a lot we don't know, says Santoshi Narayanan of the UTMD Anderson Cancer Center.
We need to do more research and understand how we can use it,
like which patients benefit from which type of mushroom.
In addition, some dieticians recommend a few nutrition basics,
like eating more fiber or protein or eating out less often before taking supplements.
For NPR News, I'm Ari Daniel.
Honda is recalling almost a million vehicles due to safety concerns about Takata airbags.
These include several models from 2012 and 13.
I'm Louise Kivoni, NPR News.
Unregulated merchant cash advances are trapping small businesses in crushing debt.
One business owner learned the hard way.
This plan only works on naive and honest people.
On The Sunday Story, inside the unregulated world of merchant cash advances.
The Sunday Story from the Up First podcast, listen now on the NPR app.

topics.text: Nvidia reinstates CEO Jensen Huang after resignation over affair with Megaspeed executive
Commerce Department blacklists Megaspeed over suspected illegal access to Nvidia chips
Poland asks NATO for stronger air defenses after Russian missiles land on its territory
NATO to send Poland an AWACS early warning aircraft, says commander Grinkewicz
Realtor.com report: about a third of 18-to-34-year-olds live with parents
AAA expects 81 million Americans to travel over Thanksgiving, nearly 6 million by air
Stormy weather and king tides threaten flooding along the U.S. West Coast
Study review finds medicinal mushrooms show promise but more research is needed
Honda recalls nearly a million vehicles over Takata airbag safety concerns
Unregulated merchant cash advances trap small businesses in crushing debt, Sunday Story reports
